rounds.text: The most compelling evidence for a turnaround is the 28% compounded sales growth achieved over the last three years [E14], which significantly outperforms the sector median sales growth of 18.3% [E45]. This recent momentum suggests the company has successfully pivoted toward a higher growth trajectory despite long-term historical declines [E12, E13]. Furthermore, the company is demonstrating exceptional capital efficiency with an ROE of 54.77%, which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 10.75% [E8]. While the market currently prices the stock at a negative book value [E1], this high return on equity indicates that the underlying operations are generating substantial value relative to their current equity base. Conceded: [E7, E15, E40, E41]. The current market capitalization of ₹ 10.8 Cr [E2] leaves significant room for re-evaluation should the recent three-year growth trend prove more durable than the trailing twelve-month volatility [E14, E15].

Incon Engineers Ltd carries severe structural and operational risks that are masked by superficial metrics. The company's most alarming vulnerability is its catastrophic asset destruction, highlighted by a staggering Return on Assets of -94.55% against a sector benchmark of just 6.14% [E7]. This fundamental failure to generate returns from assets accompanies a terminal long-term top-line decay, evidenced by compounded sales growth contracting by 6% over 10 years, 36% over 5 years, and a devastating 83% over the trailing twelve months [E12, E13, E15]. Furthermore, recent screening identifies an absolute collapse with year-over-year sales down by 100% and decelerating earnings growth [E40, E41]. Speculative momentum has completely detached from underlying business reality, as demonstrated by recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 169% [E35]. Conceded: the company displays a high Return on Equity of 54.77% and a recent 3-year compounded sales growth of 28% [E8, E14].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is -83% [E15], and year-over-year sales are down 100% according to screen reasons [E40]. However, the bear's claim of terminal top-line decay ignores the strong medium-term recovery where compounded sales growth over 3 years reaches 28% [E14]. While the bear highlights a negative Return on Assets of -94.55% [E7], this asset contraction coexists with an elite Return on Equity of 54.77%, which massively outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.75% [E8]. Furthermore, the panic over speculative momentum outpacing profit growth by 169% [E35] overlooks the broader sectoral tailwind, given that the sector median sales growth stands at a robust 18.3% [E45] to support a turnaround.

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years reaches 28% [E14], and sector median sales growth stands at 18.3% [E45]. However, that brief 3-year window is entirely overwhelmed by a catastrophic trailing twelve month sales collapse of -83% [E15] and a year-over-year sales contraction of -100% [E40], exposing the 3-year metric as an isolated blip rather than a sustainable trend. The bull's reliance on an elite Return on Equity of 54.77% [E8] is a mathematical artifact of a deeply negative book value of -1.80 yielding a bizarre price-to-book ratio of -13.89x [E1], completely masking the reality of a devastating Return on Assets of -94.55% [E7]. Furthermore, appealing to sector tailwinds to justify a turnaround ignores that price growth has raced ahead of profit growth by 169% [E35], meaning speculative expectations are entirely disconnected from fundamentals while earnings growth actively decelerates [E41].
